title: Daily issue · news clip (beta)
content: Same news clip as Set A in the daily player. Treat it as context between reading the five curations. Adjust intensity; stop for pain or dizziness.
health_review_body:
Educational only; not medical advice. Outbound links open in your system browser, not in-app (Seeker never embeds third-party pages).

① Longevity escape velocity (LEV) — "Close enough" that the next years could deliver a stack of medical breakthroughs vs. the last few decades. Still grounded: your behavior today is what you control; hype doesn't replace your clinician.

② Plank & core "killers" — Anti-extension planks and bracing beat endless flexion when the goal is a useful midline. Quality > duration for most people.

③ Strength + cardio + HIIT — Not "pick one": bone and muscle (strength), heart and mitochondria (aerobic work), and sharp intervals (metabolic) each do different jobs for longevity. Skipping steady aerobic work has a cost for many goals.

④ Food, hormones, skin, gut — What you eat most days nudges energy, skin, and digestion. Patterns beat single superfoods: enough protein, fiber, sleep, and hydration; minimize ultra-processed if that fits you.

⑤ Parkinson's & cell therapy (news) — Phase work on cell approaches is worth following as science, not as self-treatment. #longevity and neuro research move fast; rely on primary sources and your care team for any decision.

title: Daily issue · news clip (beta)
content: News clip for the daily issue player (separate from the sprint exercise verification video). Same movement ideas below still apply as general guidance. Adjust to your capacity.
health_review_body:
Educational only; not medical advice. Open links in your browser (system) — we don't embed X or other sites in-app.

① The bridge (LEV) — You don't have to "solve" aging this year. Staying in the game (sleep, safety, training that fits you) keeps optionality for better tools in the 2030s. One job: avoid needless risk; stack what keeps you strong and mobile.

② Grip & forearms — "Iron fist" is shorthand for resilient hands and forearms: carrying, holding, and joint confidence. Prefer short, quality work over grinders that wreck tomorrow's session.

③ Pelvic floor — A coordinated floor supports core stability, pressure control, and confident movement. Technique and breathing often beat over-squeezing. Persistent symptoms: ask a qualified clinician.

④ Heart "age" & research — LAV–BPIFB4 and related work are part of how science maps cardiac aging; polygenic readouts group many small genetic hints. What you still control: activity, sleep, blood pressure, nutrition — the usual levers.

⑤ Core under load — Marine-style inspo: a braced midline for pushes, pulls, carries. Favor anti-extension/rotation; if your back or neck objects, scale range or load, don't grit through.
